claude.label: Claude
claude.description: Base seat. Same delegation law as the role seats: Paseo seats are the only delegation surface, no in-session subagents.

supervisor.label: Supervisor-of-record
supervisor.description: Governance front door, process memory, Paseo lifecycle

codex-supervisor.label: Codex Supervisor
codex-supervisor.description: Supervisor seat on Codex (owner request 2026-11-05), one model: gpt-6-astra through the host's CLIProxyAPI. Carries roles/supervisor.md as developer_instructions through codex/supervisor.config.toml (room_instructions_file), the same law the Claude supervisor seat gets. Holds the Paseo tools: mcp__paseo is deliberately absent from disallowedTools, because Paseo lifecycle operation is the Supervisor's function. DIFFERENCES FROM THE CLAUDE SUPERVISOR: no role-gate.sh (a Claude Code hook) and no Paseo plan mode - Codex modes are auto, auto-review and full-access - so the no-write boundary of a no-write mandate rests on the role law, not on a mode. RUNS UNSANDBOXED (owner directive 2026-11-05): options sets sandbox_mode danger-full-access and approval_policy never; Paseo deep-merges provider options into every launch and explicit Codex sandbox/approval options override the mode presets, so the seat runs without a sandbox or approval prompts whatever mode it is created in. Measured the same day: under the auto preset every Paseo MCP call waited for a Human approval and the paseo CLI failed in the sandbox (uv_uptime EPERM), so a sandboxed Codex Supervisor cannot observe or operate. The thinking options match codex-peer's gpt-6-astra (medium default; ultra rejected by CLIProxyAPI). gpt-6-astra is off the Codex catalog; its entry is in the host's ~/.codex/model-catalog.1m.json. Fast mode stays off: do not pass featureValues.fast_mode to create_agent here.

lead.label: Lead-of-record
lead.description: Router and binding arbiter — planning, coordination, acceptance

peer.label: Peer
peer.description: Independent engineering peer; disposition (Engineer/Architect/Reviewer/Scout) set per task brief. Owner directive 2026-09-12: fast mode stays OFF on this seat too. Here it means the Claude toggle - a different feature from the Codex one on codex-peer, same id, and it was already off on every peer seat. Paseo exposes no provider key that hides it: the Claude provider surfaces it for any model whose manifest carries supportsFastMode, which is every Opus entry below. Dropping the Opus models is the only way to make the toggle disappear and the owner declined that, so the peer keeps Opus and this line is the record.

codex-peer.label: Codex Peer
codex-peer.description: Bounded engineering collaborator on CLIProxy-routed models; no Paseo tools. Six models: deepseek-v4.1-flash (the default), gpt-6-sol, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-luna. The list is the same on every host; which of them a host can serve depends on the accounts behind its CLIProxyAPI (README, Host notes), and a model the host does not serve fails at seat launch. Which role a model plays is set per workspace by that workspace's WORKSPACE_PROTOCOL.md, not here. deepseek-v4.1-flash is the declared default in BOTH this table and codex/peer.config.toml, so the model a seat resolves to and the model its record names are the same value; keep those two in step. NO OCR COVERAGE LANE (owner directive 2026-09-14): the OCR block was removed from the peer overlay and ~/.opencodereview is no longer a writable root, so a gpt-5.6-luna seat is an ordinary Peer; its thinkingOptions still offer only max. PEER DEFAULTS (owner directive 2026-09-14, from the reference Peer config): effort medium, sandbox danger-full-access, approval never. deepseek-v4.1-flash (Mistral deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017) offers high (the default), none, low, xhigh and max, the efforts Mistral accepts (2026-11-11); Mistral rejects minimal and medium, so CLIProxyAPI clamps the overlay's medium to a declared level. gpt-5.6-sol offers medium (the default, matching the overlay), low, high, xhigh and max; ultra is left out because it delegates tasks automatically. gpt-6-sol, gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-astra offer the same five levels; CLIProxyAPI rejects ultra for them outright. All three are off the Codex catalog, so their entries live in codex/peer.catalog-extra.json and the host's ~/.codex/model-catalog.1m.json. gpt-6.1-sol is the image lane where the host's [model_providers.cliproxy] carries an x-openai-actor-authorization header: Codex exposes its built-in image_gen tool only then (codex-rs image_generation_available), and codex-room-sync carries that table into the peer runtime. FAST MODE STAYS OFF (owner directive 2026-09-12): Codex fast_mode is 'Priority inference at 2x usage' and was found ON for gpt-5.6-sol on three live seats. It defaults to off, so each was turned on deliberately at spawn - do not pass featureValues.fast_mode to create_agent here.

gemini.label: Gemini
gemini.description: Base Gemini seat (owner request 2026-11-13), launched exactly like gemini-supervisor: agy-acp with the same PATH, AGY_MODELS roster and --dangerously-skip-permissions, and the Paseo MCP on (supportsMcpServers=true), like the claude and codex base seats. Models come live from `agy models`, filtered by AGY_MODELS. As on every agy-acp seat: no role law (an ACP seat takes no system prompt), no permission modes, and disallowedTools would be dropped by Paseo's acp branch, so the claude base seat's no-subagent line is not enforced here. Host prerequisites are in README, Gemini seats (agy).

gemini-peer.label: Gemini Peer
gemini-peer.description: Bounded engineering/scout collaborator on Gemini via the agy-acp ACP bridge. Mirrors codex-peer's shape: no Paseo tools. Enforced by params.supportsMcpServers=false, which is the ONLY lever that works here - `disallowedTools:['mcp__paseo']`, the mechanism used on peer and codex-peer, does not reach an ACP client. MCP is therefore all-or-nothing on this seat, and it is off. Built on Paseo's generic ACP branch (extends:'acp' -> GenericACPAgentClient). THREE PROPERTIES OF THAT BRANCH ARE LOAD-BEARING AND WERE VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED SOURCE, not assumed: (1) the acp branch builds its client from {logger,command,env,providerId,label,providerParams} only, so `disallowedTools` on this entry would be silently DROPPED - it is deliberately absent here rather than present and inert; (2) the derived definition carries modes:[] and defaultModeId:null, so this seat has NO permission modes - plan-mode pinning is unavailable and the ACP agent's own prompt flow is the only gate; (3) neither acp-agent.js nor generic-acp-agent.js reads systemPrompt or appendSystemPrompt, so ~/.paseo/orchestration/roles/*.md CANNOT be injected into this seat by any Paseo mechanism. A seat here therefore carries no role law, no role-gate.sh (a Claude Code PreToolUse hook), and no ~/.claude/skills surface. PREREQUISITE, MET 2026-09-13: agy (antigravity) 1.2.2 mac_arm64 is installed at ~/.local/bin/antigravity with an `agy` symlink; agy-acp is built from ~/.local/src/agy-acp and installed at ~/.local/bin/agy-acp. Verified end to end on that date: ACP initialize, session/new, and a full session/prompt turn that streamed an agent_message_chunk and closed with stopReason=end_turn. `env.PATH` above is load-bearing - agy-acp spawns the CLI as a bare Command::new("agy") (adapter.rs:57,634) resolved from PATH, and the daemon's own PATH does not carry ~/.local/bin. The earlier concern that this machine's conversation store was the wrong format is RESOLVED and was a false alarm: ~/.gemini/antigravity/ is the Antigravity IDE (protobuf), a different product; the CLI created ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/ (SQLite) on first run, which is exactly what agy-acp reads. Auth needed no owner action - the CLI inherited an existing Google sign-in on first invocation. No `models` array is declared on purpose - the ACP catalog is populated at runtime from `agy models`, and inventing ids here would put a guess where a live catalogue belongs.

watcher.label: Watcher
watcher.description: Read-only Watcher on Gemini, started and fed only by the Supervisor (roles/supervisor.md, Watcher section). Built on the agy-acp ACP bridge like gemini-peer, so roles/*.md cannot be injected by Paseo; instead AGY_EXTRA_ARGS adds @HOME@/.paseo/watcher to every agy run, and agy loads that directory's AGENTS.md (-> roles/watcher.md) as rules and its .agents/hooks.json as a PreToolUse gate (watcher/watcher-gate.sh). The gate, not the prompt, is the boundary: every tool is denied except run_command of paseo ls|logs|inspect, so the seat cannot read or write files, run other commands, or message seats. --dangerously-skip-permissions is required because a hook allow does not grant headless permission; the hook deny still wins (verified 2026-09-30). The directory must stay outside any git repository: agy walks from it to the repo root and would load that repo's AGENTS.md too (verified with the room checkout). No Paseo MCP (supportsMcpServers=false).

glm.label: GLM (Z.ai)
glm.description: GLM models via Z.ai Anthropic-compatible endpoint; key in ~/.paseo/glm.key

glm-researcher.label: Researcher
glm-researcher.description: Feynman research agent (github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman) run by Pi, on GLM through the Z.ai Coding Plan or on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the local CLIProxyAPI (Mistral upstream, deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017). Labelled "Researcher" since 2026-11-11 (owner request); the provider id stays glm-researcher so existing agents keep resolving. bin/pi-feynman starts pi with Feynman's system prompt, ZAI_API_KEY from ~/.paseo/glm.key and CLIPROXY_API_KEY (daemon environment, else the proxy config); the cliproxy provider is declared host-locally in ~/.pi/agent/models.json with store and the developer role turned off, both of which Mistral rejects (422). Feynman 0.5.36 and its core Pi packages (pi-subagents, pi-web-access, pi-docparser, pi-btw) are installed in ~/.pi/agent with `pi install`, and ~/.pi/agent/settings.json carries the subagent wiring the feynman launcher would write. Use /deepresearch, /lit, /review, /compare, /summarize; artifacts land in outputs/ and papers/ under the agent's cwd (~/research is set up for this). /deepresearch writes a plan and waits for a "yes" before it searches. Peer-shaped with no Paseo tools: Paseo hands its MCP to a Pi seat only when the pi-mcp-adapter extension is installed (PiRpcAgentClient.prepareMcpConfig), and disallowedTools is not read by the Pi client, so the barrier is that adapter's absence; smoke checks it. Pi has no permission modes. GLM-5.3 accepts thinking low, high and max only; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Mistral accepts off (sent as none), low, high, xhigh and max.
